cand.title: Digital History Switzerland Conference 2027
cand.excerpt: Strong official event evidence and credible scientific/education demand mechanism; venue commitment prevents treating it as open inventory.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Verified organizing-committee members: Béatrice Joyeux-Prunel (UNIGE), Radu Suciu (UNIGE), and Jérôme Baudry (EPFL). Joyeux-Prunel and Suciu are the most direct Geneva-side relationship entry points; Baudry is the EPFL co-organizer. Commercial relevance is inferred from committee membership. None is publicly identified as the accommodation buyer, procurement signatory or room-block controller.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed activity dates: 6–8 September 2027, University of Geneva, Geneva, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland; within the requested horizon. The official EPFL event listing independently confirms these dates. The 1 December 2026 date is the proposal deadline, not the conference. An organizer message dated 11 November 2026 reconfirms the edition. No later edition was identified.
findings.hotelProductFit: Assessment using the supplied hotel brief: low primary-event fit because the 2027 conference is committed to a Geneva university venue while YOTEL is in Founex, not downtown. A city-campus conference is not evidence of resort/retreat demand. Conditional fit only for independently sourced satellite lodging, an organizer/speaker subgroup, or a separately requested ancillary workshop. No published attendance supports a size match, a 20–120-room block or use of the whole 237-room hotel. Do not propose moving the main conference or assume banquet/catering capacity. No edition-specific evidence establishes Geneva Airport arrivals, La Côte lodging or willingness to commute.
findings.venueCommitments: Official wording: “The event will be hosted by the University of Geneva from September 6-8, 2027.” Published host venue: University of Geneva. Exact building, street address and rooms are not published in the reviewed edition materials. Destination classification: Geneva city, not Founex/Nyon/La Côte/Geneva Airport corridor. This is a public host commitment, not evidence of an executed venue contract or any hotel commitment.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified sequence: 12–13 September 2024, University of Basel, Basel; 6–8 September 2027, University of Geneva, Geneva, explicitly called the second edition. The 2024 final guide identifies Kollegienhaus, Petersplatz 1; Vesalianum, Vesalgasse 1; and lunch-break events at Rosshofgasse 2. This demonstrates a change of university/city, not an annual pattern, fixed three-year cycle or open future host competition.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. The 2027 practical-information section states only: “The conference is organized jointly by the Laboratory for the history of science and technology (EPFL) and the Digital Humanities Chair (University of Geneva). The event will be hosted by the University of Geneva from September 6-8, 2027.” Reviewed English/French/German materials and the EPFL listing identify no housing bureau, incumbent hotel, hotel list, room block, booking code or hotel RFP. No hotels can therefore be named as edition-specific lodging commitments. Silence does not establish open or independently booked accommodation.
findings.organizationStructure: Academic co-organization, not a corporate event or identified PCO-led programme: EPFL Laboratory for the History of Science and Technology and UNIGE Digital Humanities Chair. Infoclio describes collaboration/co-organization in its announcement; the host CFP lists the two academic units and names the three-person organization committee. No agency, PCO, DMC or contracted housing intermediary is identified. Permanent series ownership and contracting entity remain unverified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The university host commitment limits main-meeting capture but is not a competing-hotel lodging commitment. No edition-specific incumbent hotels, contracted housing bureau, sold-out hotels, overflow demand or unmet room requirement were identified. Geographic convenience for the campus is a likely competitive disadvantage for Founex (inference); no quantified travel-time or hotel-price advantage is claimed.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Radu Suciu and Béatrice Joyeux-Prunel through the published conference mailbox, digital-history-2027@unige.ch, explicitly asking for referral to the accommodation/logistics decision-maker; it is a CFP mailbox, not a proven sales/procurement channel. Ask whether lodging is centralized, which hotels/bureau are committed, the exact campus, nonlocal attendance and peak nights, and whether a Founex satellite option is acceptable. Only after affirmative qualification offer a small, demand-led room allocation; discuss ancillary meeting space only if separately requested. Revisit after the published mid-February 2027 acceptance notifications if demand is still being defined. Deprioritize if housing is centrally committed or participants require walkable Geneva lodging.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the selected upcoming 2027 edition, meeting-venue access is constrained by the announced university host. Hotel sourcing is unconfirmed, not verified open and not verified committed elsewhere. No published attendance, expected overnight share, peak rooms or room nights were located. Treat as qualification/relationship outreach only until the lodging pathway and willingness to stay outside central Geneva are confirmed.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: the Basel-to-Geneva sequence supports maintaining organizer relationships for possible later workshops or editions. It does not establish a future destination, date, hotel tender or recurring room allocation. No post-2027 edition announcement was identified. Do not publish a later-cycle room opportunity or infer a 2030 edition.
